title: Reflexivity in Options Markets: A Stochastic-Volatility Model with Dealer-Gamma Feedback, Hopf Bifurcation Calculus, and a Pre-Registered Evaluation Framework
description: A continuous-time Heston-like stochastic-volatility model in which the underlying spot price is coupled to its own option market through a dealer-gamma feedback channel, derived from the open-interest grid via a Garleanu-Pedersen-Poteshman (2009) demand-pressure mapping. The model state is three-dimensional: spot S_t, instantaneous variance v_t, and a low-pass-filtered log-spot memory variable z_t; it reduces to standard time-dependent Heston at zero coupling. The contribution is the synthesis of three previously separate ingredients into a single analytical and computational object: (i) a continuous-time SV backbone with explicit dealer-gamma drift, (ii) a formal Hopf bifurcation calculus on the deterministic skeleton with first Lyapunov coefficient ell_1 and Khasminskii-style stochastic shift Lambda, and (iii) a pre-registered evaluation protocol for RL-trained hedging agents trained inside the simulator. For a representative dimensionless calibration the critical coupling is kappa* approx 0.8964, angular frequency omega* approx 0.5724 rad/yr, and first Lyapunov coefficient ell_1 approx -0.025 < 0, so the bifurcation is supercritical: an attracting limit cycle in volatility is born for kappa > kappa*. The 2D reduction (without z_t) has an upper-triangular Jacobian and admits only a saddle-node onset, recovering the discrete-time recursion of Dai (2025); the 3D extension is what unlocks the Hopf. For the natural parametric specification with log-normal open-interest in moneyness, a closed-form Hopf threshold and a closed-form ell_1 are obtained, exposing a parametric phase boundary in (sigma_q, gamma) space. This Zenodo deposit archives the software, manuscript PDF, and pre-registration anchor that accompany the paper.
